newsitem.title: HUNGARY: INTERVIEW - UK aims to double C.Euro trade by 1998.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - UK aims to double C.Euro trade by 1998.

text.p: The UK launched an 18-month campaign aimed at doubling British exports to central Europe to an annual four billion stg by 1998, a government official said on Thursday.
"We aim to double our trade and to inspire 100 new investment projects before the end of next year," British Trade Minister Anthony Nelson told Reuters in an interview.
He launched in Budapest the Department of Trade and Industry's (DTI) "Open for Business" project aimed at five central European countries, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, Slovakia and Slovenia.
"I expect to see Hungary in pole position amongst those countries to benefit from a new access in our bilateral trade and investment," Nelson said.
He said trade between the UK and Hungary is likely to exceed $1 billion in 1997 and that British companies have so far invested another billion of investments in Hungary.
"Today I will be opening a new Glaxo-Wellcome factory which is just one example of the capital investment as well as the current trade that is going on," he said.
He pinpointed the agricultural business, automotive, electronics and telecommunications industry, consumer goods and healthcare as the five sectors on which the campaign will concentrate.
Since 1990, Hungary has attracted over $13 billion of foreign direct investment, with Germany leading the investors' list with some 25 percent of the total.
Nelson said the DTI initiative was in harmony with the European Union's economic agenda concerning the five countries and added that Britain will support Hungary's bid for membership.
"Britain intends to be Hungary's champion in joining the EU," he said. "We hope that the timetable can be accelerated and agreement reached".
He added that NATO and EU membership prospects are likely to attract foreign investors to Hungary.
"The two are inextricably linked and I believe they will give encouragement and momentum to new trade and investment," Nelson said.
He said, however, that there are some barriers in the way of expanding bilateral trade he hopes can be solved during his meeting with Hungarian officials.
"I will also be looking at...the question of tariffs, access to the European Union, procurement by government," Nelson said. "I very much hope that we can clear the way".
Choosing Hungary as the first stop of his promotional trip can be interpreted as a message, he said.
"For too long, the image of trade between our two countries has been 'distant and difficult'" Nelson said. "I believe it is now 'bright and new'".
